newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris restaurant had British beef despite ban.
newsitem.headline: Paris restaurant had British beef despite ban.

text.p: French police seized 300 kg (660 lbs) of frozen British beef from a Paris restaurant under laws banning British beef because of the mad cow crisis, police sources said on Thursday.

The frozen hamburgers were found during a routine health check at the Hard Rock Cafe on the Boulevard Montmartre in central Paris, one of an international American-style chain owned by the Rank Organisation.
"The batch of frozen minced beef had a stamp indicating an English origin," Jean Jamet, head of veterinary services at Paris police headquarters, told Reuters.

The Hard Rock Cafe declined immediate comment, saying it was preparing a statement. Jamet said the restaurant argued that it had acted in good faith and the meat, discovered on Tuesday, would be incinerated.

The haul was the largest in the capital since France banned imports and marketing of British beef in March over fears that mad cow disease, or Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), could be passed to humans. BSE is most widespread in Britain.
Under French law, importers of the meat could face legal action and the restaurant could risk a temporary closure.
